newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Put buying dominates Bunds, futures rally.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Put buying dominates Bunds, futures rally.

text.p: A spurt upwards in Bund futures on Friday led to concerns a correction may soon be on the cards and pushed up Bund option put buying, traders on LIFFE said.
Puts were bid up after the underlying June Bund future broke above the 102.00 level. The futures reached a high of 102.14 earlier and were trading up 0.29 at 102.00 by 1035 GMT.

"The futures market is perceived to be at the top of its range," said a trader at a French brokerage on LIFFE. "A lot of people are now looking for a correction and are buying protection against that."
Implied volatility of June options rose to 4.9 percent from 4.8 percent, but traders said the proximity of June's expiry was skewing vol. June options expire in 13 days.

In September options on the September future the volatility was steady at 5.3 percent. Traders said most activity was in buying puts and selling calls. German institutions were active although volume was not great.

A trader at a British brokerage said a break of 102.00 had been key, sending investors looking for a hedge into the options. However there was no sign volatility was going to break above the 5.5 percent cap it has recently set up.
